title: Event Onramp Hygiene and Schema Sentinel for Console Usage Pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight Schema Sentinel service in the Console backend that sits in the usage event onramp. The sentinel performs low-latency validation, graceful coercions for common shape errors, and an adaptive backpressure signal for noisy tenants. This reduces downstream pipeline failures, improves SLOs for ingest latency, and provides actionable telemetry for PM/Support teams.

Background: Recent incidents (see incident report link below) showed binary failures in the analytics pipeline caused by unexpected optional fields and malformed arrays. Current fallback logic in the consumer layer is too late (after enrichment & joins), causing wasted compute and alert storms. A focused onramp gate will catch these early with minimal impact to well-formed traffic.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Validate canonical event schema at the onramp with <2ms median added latency for well-formed events.
- Soft-coerce: coerce stringified numbers and ISO timestamps when safe; attach a 'coercion' reason tag.
- Quarantine vs Reject: reject clearly invalid payloads (schema-breaking types), quarantine ambiguous events into a dead-letter stream with sampling for analysis.
- Tenant-level adaptive backpressure: when a tenant exceeds error-rate thresholds or throughput budget, apply token-bucket throttling and emit remediation reasons to the client.
- Expose metrics and traces in Console: per-route error counts, coercion rates, latency percentiles, and current tenant throttle state.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Inline validation vs sidecar: we opted for an inline Rust microservice (fast path) to avoid cross-process network hops. This keeps added latency low but means rollout must be conservative; canary with traffic split required.
- Soft coercion policy: to avoid silent data corruption, coercions will be annotated and surfaced in the Console UI; PMs will be able to opt into an automatic correction policy per-tenant.
- Backpressure signals are conservative: first apply a 429 with Retry-After and explanatory error codes, then fall back to sample-dropping for sustained overload.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype validation library with declarative schema rules (JSON Schema + lightweight custom rules for kv-typed fields). Store rule-sets in a small ConfigMap with hash-based versioning.
2) Implement sentinel microservice with a hot-path validator, metrics, and a rate-limiter per-tenant.
3) Canary: route 0.5% of production traffic in a single region, observe latency and false-positive rates for 48h.
4) Dashboard: add per-tenant ingestion health to Console (coercion trends, rejections, throttle events).
5) Rollout: staged expansion to all regions and then enable optional adaptive correction policy.

Monitoring & Rollback:
- Key metrics: ingress.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), ingress.coercion_rate, ingress.reject_rate, tenant.throttle_ratio.
- Automated rollback triggers: p99 latency increase > 10% for 15m; reject_rate spike > 0.2% absolute for >30m.

Security & Compliance:
- Contains no PII extraction; dead-letter stream encrypted at rest and ACL-protected. KMS keys per-environment.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/Onramp+Schema+Sentinel
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/console/onramp-sentinel-design-v1.pdf
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6241
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/console-onramp/canary

Notes: This ticket focuses on the common path validator and throttling. Integrations (DLQ consumer analysis tooling, PM-facing corrections UI) will be separate follow-ups.

2026-03-07 - QA (Nora): Ran schema fuzz tests against historical week of events; coercion rate ~0.14% and reject rate 0.03%. We'll need a small whitelist for legacy mobile SDKs.
2026-03-09 - Security (Priya): Reviewed DLQ encryption and KMS usage. Recommend adding audit log hook for manual DLQ access. Adding security_review_required flag.

2026-03-11 - Marco: Canary started (0.5% traffic). Observed slight p99 latency drift in us-east (up 8%) correlated with large batched payloads. Tuning validator to short-circuit big-array checks. Next: increase canary to 2% after tuning.
